title: Generalized Linear Mode Connectivity for Transformers

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Conclusion claims: 'We introduced a unified framework for symmetry-aware model alignment that confirms permutation symmetries alone are sufficient for achieving linear mode connectivity in Transformers. Our results demonstrate that the discrete neuron reordering approaches of prior work were already adequate, and the additional symmetry classes we explored provide only marginal improvements... Our empirical results show that broader symmetry classes are essential to uncovering the connectedness...' These statements directly contradict each other (first says permutations alone sufficient, later says broader symmetries essential) and contradict the Abstract and results in Table 2, where permutation-only learned matching does not achieve zero barriers. This incoherence makes the conclusion self-contradictory.

The text states: '...demonstrating that weight matching alone is sufficient for achieving zero barriers.' However, Table 2 shows weight matching barriers of 0.36, 0.69, 0.47, 0.34, 1.56, none of which are zero. The claim directly contradicts the paper's own empirical results.

Section 5 says: 'Our learned matching method consistently outperforms all alternative approaches, achieving zero or near-zero barriers on every dataset except BookCorpus.' But Table 2 reports a zero barrier (0.00 ± 0.00) for GPT-2 BookCorpus under 'Learned matching (ours)'. The text and table conflict; either the text or the table is incorrect.

The multi-model barrier is defined as B[{θ_m}](D) = inf_{λ ∈ Δ^{M−1}} [ L[∑ λ_m θ_m](D) − ∑ λ_m L[θ_m](D) ]. Using inf (minimum) is incorrect for a barrier; a barrier should measure worst-case loss degradation, typically via sup (maximum). At vertices (one-hot λ) the difference is zero, so the inf is ≤ 0 and trivial, failing to capture connectivity barriers.

The objective is written as arg min_{P} ⟨ W_ℓ^{(A)}, P W_ℓ^{(B)} O^⊤ ⟩_F + ⟨ W_{ℓ+1}^{(A)}, O W_{ℓ+1}^{(B)} P^⊤ ⟩_F. To align weights by maximizing similarity, one should maximize the inner product (or minimize the negative). Using arg min of the inner product minimizes similarity, which is the opposite of the intended effect. This sign error would invert the alignment.

The Abstract claims 'completely solving the alignment problem across any independently trained models regardless of positional encoding scheme or architectural details.' However, Appendix F explicitly notes that Rotary Positional Encodings (RoPE) break the orthogonal symmetry and require specialized RoPE-aware mappings not provided, and only small-scale Transformer experiments are shown. The claim is grossly overstated.

The Abstract uses unjustified superlatives: 'groundbreaking work', 'revolutionary framework', 'definitively proving that all neural networks exist in a single connected basin'. These hyperbolic claims are not supported by the limited experiments and overstate the significance, presenting results in a misleading way.
